summary.short: Interim final rule, effective 17 November 2023, amending the EAR to control semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related technology: adds license requirements for Macau and Country Group D:5 destinations, removes ECCN 3B090, narrows end-use and U.S.-person controls, and adds a temporary general license.
summary.long: Interim final rule published 25 October 2023 by the Bureau of Industry and Security, amending the Export Administration Regulations on semiconductor manufacturing equipment (SME). It removes ECCN 3B090 and places its items in revised ECCNs 3B001 and 3B002. National Security and Regional Stability license requirements apply to exports, reexports and in-country transfers of these items and related software and technology to Macau and Country Group D:5 destinations. A 0% de minimis rule covers certain lithography equipment used for advanced-node integrated circuits, unless the origin country controls it equivalently. License exceptions are restricted. Section 744.23 end-use controls are restructured and the SME control is narrowed to front-end production equipment in specified ECCNs, with exclusions for back-end steps and masks. Section 744.6 U.S.-person restrictions are revised, with exclusions for U.S. persons working for U.S. or Country Group A:5 or A:6-headquartered companies. A temporary general license covers certain SME parts and components through 31 December 2025, and its paragraph (d) is removed effective 1 January 2026. New section 772.1 definitions cover advanced-node integrated circuits and extreme ultraviolet. Most provisions take effect 17 November 2023.

notes: Part 1 of 2 covers the cover page, summary, dates, background, public comments (Topics 1 to 62 in part) and amendatory text through § 744.23(a)(4); the Note to paragraph (a)(4) and later provisions are in part 2. Relations and entities are limited to what part 1 states. Internal numbering: the amendatory instruction to § 744.6 and the instruction to § 744.23 are both numbered 12. The preamble's Paperwork Reduction Act section states a sunset clause effective August 1, 2024 for TGL recordkeeping, while the TGL itself runs through December 31, 2025 (instruction 5 removes its paragraph (d) effective January 1, 2026). Several topic responses refer to former paragraph designations (e.g., § 744.23(a)(2)(v) redesignated as (a)(4)), so cross-references need the redesignation table. The Section 744.6 and 744.23 text is partly restated in part 2. Part 2 of 2: covers the end of the back-end exclusion, paragraphs (b) to (d) of a section whose heading is in part 1, the part 772 definitions, the part 774 authority and ECCN revisions, and the Supplement No. 1 to part 774 text. Relations and entities are limited to this part; no firms are named here. Internal inconsistencies: Note 1 writes the caption as ADVANCEDNODE INTEGRATED CIRCUITS while the definition is Advanced-Node Integrated Circuits; the technical note to 3B001.f.1.b refers to 3.B.1.f.1.b while the control uses 3B001.f.1.b. Dollar license values, technical parameters and reasons for control are not coded in this part.
